Lemma
[Weighted maximum estimate on a ball] 1. ch6:6.21\group gt-ch06 If $B=B_R(x_0)$, $c\le 0$, the coefficients of $L$ are bounded by $\Lambda $, $u\in C^0(\bar B)\cap C^2(B)$ solves $Lu=f$ with $u=0$ on $\partial B$, and $0<\beta <1$, then \begin{equation} \tag {6.52} \sup _B d_x^{-\beta }|u(x)|\le C\sup _B d_x^{2-\beta }|f(x)|, \end{equation} where $C=C(\beta ,n,R,\lambda ,\Lambda )$.
Proof

\sketch Compare $u$ with a linear combination of $w_1=(R^2-|x-x_0|^2)^\beta $ and an exponential barrier. The first controls the annulus and the second controls the centre; the maximum principle gives

\begin{equation} \tag {6.53} |u(x)|\leq Nw(x)\qquad (x\in B), \end{equation}

for $N=\sup d^{2-\beta }|f|$, hence (6.52).

□
